notes: Covers what Docs/COLLAB_RESTRUCTURE_PLAN.md listed as Parts 2 AND 3 — founder: 'make it single instead of two', because an agreement with nowhere to go is not useful. Builds the pre-campaign handshake: brand-initiated requests (which do not exist today in any form), the shared terms model, the agreement record, and the handoff into campaign creation. Biggest behaviour change is a REMOVAL: accepting a pitch stops fabricating a campaign/set/assignment/contract and produces an agreement instead.

founder_decisions.two_record_types: A creator pitch and a brand request are separate records that SHARE the terms model and response flow. A pitch says 'I want to work with you'; a request says 'I want you for something'. Never converted into one another.
founder_decisions.existing_stubs: The fabricated stub campaigns already in production are left alone; the new flow carries fresh ones.
founder_decisions.agreement_expiry: Three months unbriefed, then it expires.
founder_decisions.creator_default: Creators are open to brand requests BY DEFAULT and can mute. Opt-in would leave most creators unreachable and the feature unused. Deliberately asymmetric with the brand side, which is opt-in — the two sides are not in the same position.
founder_decisions.broadcast: A filter-matched request is a ONE-TIME snapshot, not standing recruitment. Standing recruitment belongs to open sales campaigns.
founder_decisions.counter_rounds: Two counters each, then settle or drop — matching the existing campaign contract rule so both negotiations feel the same.
founder_decisions.limits_admin_controlled: Limits are NOT hardcoded. A handshake_settings row, admin-editable, following the referral_settings / world_rule_settings / follower_app_config pattern. Covers BOTH sides — leaving creator limits frozen in code while brand limits are editable would be confusing to operate. Seeded with today's values.
founder_decisions.one_agreement_one_collaboration: An agreement is one brand with one creator, consumed when briefed, so Ready to brief always shows exactly what is outstanding. Several agreements can still be briefed into ONE campaign across its sets — one agreement per whole campaign would recreate the per-creator fragmentation this contract removes.
founder_decisions.negotiate_once: All negotiation happens at the handshake. When the detailed campaign arrives, an agreement-backed creator sees settled terms locked and a single Accept that generates the contract — no Negotiate. A creator invited cold keeps today's Accept / Decline / Negotiate. Decline stays in both cases.
founder_decisions.mobile_surface: The Influencers tab in the brand app, where search, proposals and groups already live, mirroring web.
founder_decisions.maestro: Parked by founder decision, so the mobile leg is held at release.

verified_facts.brand_outreach_absent: No table and no endpoint for brand → creator requests. The only outreach is a campaign invite (needs a campaign) or an invitation to an unclaimed scraped creator (needs them to not be on the platform).
verified_facts.creator_side_built: 15 endpoints, full lifecycle, with 5 active / 3 per day / 10 per week caps, 7-day expiry, 30-day rejection cooldown, brand opt-in off by default, a brand eligibility bar, and admin suspend/ban — all currently hardcoded in proposal.service.
verified_facts.acceptance_fabricates: proposal.controller acceptance INSERTs a campaign with only (brand_id, name, status, created_at) — hence the dateless campaigns already in production — plus a set, a campaign_influencer and a contract draft.
verified_facts.accept_already_makes_contract: offer.controller accept already calls contractService.autoCreate, so the one-click requirement is mostly REMOVING the negotiate step rather than adding contract generation.
verified_facts.targeting_exists: Handpick, server-persisted creator groups with members, and a filter matcher on tier / niche (incl. secondary) / city / min engagement / gender — all working, but fired once at campaign publish.
